ASU offers direct admission for nearly all majors, which means students are directly admitted as long as they meet applicable admission requirements for both ASU and their major and complete the steps to apply.
A transfer student is anyone who has attended another college or university and has completed 12 or more transferable credits post-high school at the time of applying to Arizona State University.
The minimum GPA for transfer admission consideration at ASU is typically around 2.50.
Transfer students with 12–23 transferable credits (post-high school) must have a minimum 2.50 cumulative transfer GPA and meet first-year student admission requirements.
Applying to ASU only takes about 30 minutes.
You’ll get an admission decision within 10 days if you self-report your grades, but it may take a little longer if your transcript is sent directly.
ASU may offer conditional admission to international applicants who meet the academic requirements but are not proficient in English.
International F-1 students have three semesters to submit a passing TOEFL, IELTS, or PTE score, or to successfully graduate from ASU Global Launch to be fully admitted to the university.

value: The first step in completing the ASU undergraduate application is the My Information section.
The second section of the application focuses on your prior academic history, including high school and any colleges or universities you previously attended.
Students have the option to self-report high school grades in the My Grades section of the application, though self-reporting is not required.
The information shared in the residency portion of the undergraduate application helps determine if you are an in-state, out-of-state, or international student.
If you're unsure about what major is best for you, resources are offered to help you decide, and you can change your major later.
Review your application, submit it, and pay the application fee.

programme_facts.value: Build a Transfer Map is only available for transfer institutions within the United States and for military Joint Service Transcripts.
ASU only accepts credit from regionally accredited institutions.
Accreditation questions can be referred to your transfer institution or to ASU Admissions Services.
Students from institutions with highly unique or experimental methods of instruction are encouraged to work with an Academic Advisor or transfer specialist.
It is possible that ASU has not yet reviewed your course, or that the content of the course was determined to be insufficient or incompatible with the ASU requirement.
Additional helpful Transfer Guide tools include Course Search and Submit Course for Evaluation.
ASU does allow some courses to fulfill more than one requirement.
A single course may be used to satisfy only one core area according to ASU General Studies policy.
ASU’s Transfer Guide is a comprehensive suite of self-service online tools to show how your prior college or university credits can transfer to ASU and your major.
ASU uses the American Council on Education's Guide to the Evaluation of Educational Experiences in the Armed Services to assess how to transfer military credits to ASU.

Military credits that transfer to ASU through educational experiences in the armed services are not applicable toward completing ASU’s general studies requirements for graduation, but do count for total credits toward completion.
In many cases, older earned college credits can still be evaluated for transfer students depending on the year, subject and program.
ASU reviews coursework to determine what applies toward your degree.
In some cases, students may be required to provide a syllabus or course description to facilitate review of older coursework.
Credits are officially evaluated after admission to ASU with your academic advisor.
It is recommended the JST be sent to ASU upon application to ensure timely processing and evaluation.
A transfer student is anyone applying for admission who has attended another college or university and has completed 12 or more transferable credits post-high school, at the time of application.
If you are completing college courses while in high school you are considered a freshman and not a transfer student.
